dedupe_keys.name: resilient telecommunications infrastructure a practitioner s guide world bank 2024

description: This World Bank guide gathers reference information for planning telecom networks that withstand climate and natural hazards. Its 44 pages set out the hazards that affect connectivity infrastructure and the typical damage each causes to towers, fibre, submarine cables, data centres and power supply; resilience measures by type of infrastructure; system-level redundancy and power backup; disaster recovery, contingency and continuity planning; how to build resilience into procurement; and the enabling policy and regulation. Annexes list redundancy considerations, the main industry standards bodies and certifications, sources of hazard and risk data for screening, and resilient procurement checklists. It was produced with support from the Digital Development Partnership and draws on World Bank work including the global base station climate risk study. Coverage: global guidance for low- and middle-income countries. Format and access: PDF from the World Bank documents site, free for non-commercial reuse with attribution. Caveats: guidance, not measured data; tables are qualitative. Simulation uses: structured lists of hazard-damage mechanisms for building fragility assumptions, catalogues of resilience measures for adaptation scenarios, and a pointer list of hazard datasets. Related records: the global base station climate risk results and open-rigbi quantify exposure, and the EU 5G risk assessment covers security threats.
